name: Laryngeal Abductor Paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Laryngoscopic Diagnostic Criteria for Laryngeal Abductor Paralysis

criteria.description: Visualization of immobile vocal cord in paramedian or midline position on laryngoscopy
Electromyographic evidence of absent or reduced posterior cricoarytenoid muscle activity
Presence of inspiratory stridor exacerbated by exertion or respiratory distress
Hoarseness or breathy dysphonia due to impaired vocal cord abduction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of vocal cord immobility on laryngoscopy plus absent posterior cricoarytenoid muscle function on electromyography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of mechanical fixation or other causes of vocal cord immobility.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral vocal cord immobility in paramedian position
searchTerms: vocal cords stuck in middle position
unilateral or bilateral vocal cord paralysis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inspiratory stridor due to impaired vocal cord abduction
searchTerms: breathing noise from vocal cord blockage
inspiratory stridor due to vocal cord
airway noise from vocal cord movement

common.symptomName: Breathy dysphonia from incomplete glottic opening
searchTerms: hoarse voice from incomplete vocal cord closure

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion related to airway obstruction
Chronic cough due to impaired airway protection
searchTerms: persistent cough due to airway issues
food or liquid going into airway

occasional.symptomName: Neck discomfort or pain related to nerve injury

rare.symptomName: Bilateral vocal cord paralysis causing severe airway obstruction
searchTerms: both vocal cords paralyzed causing airway blockage
severe breathing obstruction from vocal cord paralysis

rare.symptomName: Recurrent respiratory infections secondary to aspiration
searchTerms: lung infections due to swallowing issues

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: Laryngoscopy showing immobile vocal cord(s) in paramedian position
CT or MRI to exclude structural lesions compressing recurrent laryngeal nerve
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated; usually acquired
other: Electromyography demonstrating absent or reduced posterior cricoarytenoid muscle activity
Pulmonary function tests may show variable extrathoracic airway obstruction

distinguishingFeatures: Mechanical fixation of vocal cord due to cricoarytenoid joint arthritis or scarring
No electromyographic evidence of muscle denervation
Paralysis due to nerve injury but may involve both abductors and adductors
Often associated with identifiable nerve trauma or tumor
Involves both vocal cords leading to airway obstruction
More severe respiratory symptoms and stridor

redFlags: Sudden onset of bilateral vocal cord paralysis
Signs of aspiration pneumonia or recurrent respiratory infections
references: Koufman JA. Laryngeal Paralysis: Diagnosis and Management. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2018.
Sulica L. Vocal Fold Paralysis. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2017.
